findings.summary: Page 1 ends with a Python multi-stage runtime snippet that uses `COPY --from=build` three pages before multi-stage builds, stages, or even COPY itself are introduced.
findings.evidence: Page 1 block: `["FROM python:3.12-slim","COPY --from=build /opt/venv /opt/venv","ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH","CMD [\"python\",\"-m\",\"app\"]"]` — `COPY` is first defined on page 2 ("COPY | yes | from context") and `--from=<stage>` only on pages 5–6 ("Each FROM starts a fresh stage with its own stack").
findings.fix: Delete this block from page 1 and move it to the Ch9 recipes material, where the Python slim + venv multi-stage Dockerfile belongs; page 1 should end on the "Deleted ≠ Gone" callout.

findings.summary: The caption states the carousel is ten pages, but eleven titles are listed.
findings.evidence: caption: "Ten pages, ending at 150MB with a non-root user and pinned digests." vs. titles array of 11 entries ending with "Alpine vs Slim vs Distroless vs Scratch"

findings.summary: Chapter 2's sections 3 and 4 are printed at the bottom of page 1, before sections 1 and 2 of that same chapter appear on page 2.
findings.evidence: Page 1 ends with headings "3. No Shell State Survives" and "4. Chain What Depends"; page 2 then opens with "1. One Instruction, One Layer" and "2. Ordering Is Semantic", and jumps from there to "5. COPY vs ADD".
findings.fix: Move the "3. No Shell State Survives" and "4. Chain What Depends" heading/code pairs to page 2, between "2. Ordering Is Semantic" and "5. COPY vs ADD", restoring the 1→2→3→4→5 run.

findings.summary: The claim that ADD cannot verify a checksum is outdated — BuildKit's ADD has supported `--checksum` for remote HTTP sources since Dockerfile frontend 1.5 / Docker 23.
findings.evidence: note on the `ADD https://x.io/t.tgz /tmp/  # ✗` code block: "ADD never verifies a checksum"
findings.fix: Change the note to "bare ADD never verifies; use `ADD --checksum=sha256:<hash> <url> <dest>` (BuildKit, Dockerfile 1.5+) or the curl + sha256sum -c pattern", and drop the ✗ from the ADD line or reframe it as "ADD without --checksum".

findings.summary: The cache chapter runs out of numeric order across pages: section 6 and its unnumbered follow-ups are on page 4 while sections 3, 4, 5 and a second section 6 are on page 5.
findings.evidence: Page 4 opens with "6. Context Ships First"; page 5 then runs "3. Two Consequences", "4. The Manifest Split", "5. Same Trick, Any Stack", "6. Where The Miss Starts".
findings.fix: Reflow so page 4 carries sections 3–5 (consequences, manifest split, per-stack table) and page 5 carries 6–7 (context, where the miss starts), so the reader never meets a section 6 before section 3.

findings.summary: Page 4's Q&A and rebuild table hand the learner the manifest-split and .dockerignore fixes that pages 5 and 7 are supposed to teach.
findings.evidence: Page 4 qa: "Why does a README typo reinstall every dep?" → "Fix: copy manifests first, add `.dockerignore`", while page 5 heading "4. The Manifest Split" and page 7 heading "1. Filter Before Upload" are where those are actually taught.
findings.fix: Cut the fix line from the page 4 Q&A down to a forward pointer ("the fix is the manifest split, next page"), and place the full Q&A after page 5's manifest-split section.

findings.summary: Multi-stage sections are interleaved with a leftover cache section, so the chapter reads 1, 3, 7, 2, 4, 5, 6.
findings.evidence: Page 5 ends "1. Many FROMs, One File" then "3. Go Builder Stage"; page 6 opens "7. Persist Across Builds" (BuildKit cache mounts / CI cache, chapter 3 material) and only then "2. Artifact Handoff", "4. Go Final Stage", "5. Node Split + Targets", "6. Common Stage Layout".
findings.fix: Move "7. Persist Across Builds" back to the end of the cache pages (after "6. Where The Miss Starts"), and put "2. Artifact Handoff" ahead of "3. Go Builder Stage" so the builder/runtime picture precedes the code that implements it.

findings.summary: The .dockerignore chapter opens with its section 2 diagram on page 6, and page 7 then leads with a stray multi-stage sidebox and repeats the number 7 twice.
findings.evidence: Page 6 ends with "2. What Actually Gets Sent" (context tar diagram); page 7 begins "7. Why rm Cannot Help" (a multi-stage sidebox: "`RUN make && rm -rf /build-deps` shrinks nothing") before "1. Filter Before Upload", and later carries a second "7. Three Separate Wins".
findings.fix: Move "7. Why rm Cannot Help" to page 6 with the multi-stage material, move the "2. What Actually Gets Sent" diagram onto page 7 after "1. Filter Before Upload", and renumber the second section 7 so no page has duplicate numbers.

findings.summary: The caption claims the deck ends at the 150MB build, but that is page 10 of 11 — a comparison page follows it.

findings.summary: The instruction table lists WORKDIR as metadata-only, but WORKDIR creates the directory if it is missing and therefore produces a real filesystem layer.
findings.evidence: table row: ["ENV/CMD/WORKDIR","no","config only"]
findings.fix: Move WORKDIR out of that row (e.g. "ENV/CMD/LABEL | no | config only") and add "WORKDIR | yes (tiny) | sets config *and* mkdir -p the path".

findings.summary: Metadata instructions produce no layer at all, not "zero-byte layers" — the bullet contradicts the table on the same page and implies they count toward the ~125-layer depth cap discussed two sections later.
findings.evidence: bullet: "Metadata instructions produce zero-byte layers" vs table: ["ENV/CMD/WORKDIR","no","config only"]
findings.fix: Reword to "Metadata instructions add a history entry, not a layer — no bytes and no depth cost."

findings.summary: Page 3 is a single code example whose governing rule is only stated two pages later.
findings.evidence: Page 3 contains one block, the `ARG GIT_SHA` cachebust snippet noted "declare a changing ARG just before use"; the rule "Declare a changing ARG just before its use" appears on page 5 under "3. Two Consequences".
findings.fix: Merge the ARG example onto the page that states the ARG-placement rule, so the rule and its illustration sit together.

findings.summary: An `ADD` checksum anti-pattern from the mistakes chapter is dropped into the cache page, where it answers a security question the page never raised.
findings.evidence: Page 4 code block `["ADD https://x.io/t.tgz /tmp/  # ✗", ... "| sha256sum -c -          # ✓"]` with note "ADD never verifies a checksum", between the build-log cache example and the manifest Q&A.
findings.fix: Move this block to the anti-patterns material alongside the other "secrets and downloads" items, or reframe it on page 4 to state the cache consequence of `ADD <url>` rather than checksum verification.

findings.summary: Pages 3 and 4 both advertise "Cache Keys" as their subject, so the titles do not distinguish the two pages.
findings.evidence: "Cache Keys & Where ARG Belongs" (page 3) and "Context, Cache Keys & What Busts Them" (page 4)
findings.fix: Retitle one to its distinct angle, e.g. page 3 → "What Goes Into a Cache Key (and Where ARG Belongs)" and page 4 → "The Build Context & What Busts the Cache".

findings.summary: A code line in the 'BuildKit + CI' box runs into and past the box's right border.
findings.evidence: '--mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm' extends to the green box edge, the trailing '.npm' crossing the border rule instead of wrapping inside it.
findings.fix: Allow this code line to wrap inside the box (or reduce its font size/increase box width) so no glyph crosses the border.

findings.summary: The secret-mount example would not actually authenticate npm: `--mount=type=secret,id=npm` mounts at /run/secrets/npm, which npm never reads.
findings.evidence: code: "RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npm \\", "      npm ci   # ✓ never a layer" with "--secret id=npm,src=.npmrc"
findings.fix: Add the target to the mount: `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npm,target=/root/.npmrc npm ci` (or set NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG=/run/secrets/npm).

findings.summary: BuildKit does not silently ignore `--squash`; it rejects the flag and the build fails.
findings.evidence: --squash sidebox: "Experimental ==legacy builder== flag; BuildKit ignores it"
findings.fix: Replace with "Experimental legacy-builder flag; buildx/BuildKit rejects it — the build errors out and points you at multi-stage".

findings.summary: A non-root user code block sits unlabelled at the end of the size page, while the section that explains it is on the next page.
findings.evidence: Page 9's last block is `["RUN adduser -S -u 10001 app","COPY --chown=10001 dist/ /app/","USER 10001:10001   # numeric = safe"]`, immediately after the "--squash" sidebox; page 10 then has heading "8. Never Ship As Root" with the bullets that justify it.
findings.fix: Move the adduser/USER code block to page 10 directly beneath "8. Never Ship As Root".

findings.summary: The base-image decision table asks the learner to choose on `musl` and `distroless`, terms not explained until the final page.
findings.evidence: Page 9 table rows: "alpine | ~7MB | musl is fine" and "distroless | ~2MB | prod, no shell"; musl and distroless are first explained on page 11 ("Alpine ships musl and BusyBox, not glibc and GNU coreutils", "Your app plus runtime deps and CA certs. Nothing else").
findings.fix: Add a one-line gloss in the page 9 table caption (musl = Alpine's lighter libc; distroless = runtime files only, no shell) plus a pointer to the comparison page, or move the base-image comparison page ahead of the shrinking page.

findings.summary: Distroless images do ship an /etc/passwd (root, nobody, nonroot at UID 65532), so the bullet lumping distroless with scratch is wrong.
findings.evidence: "scratch/distroless have no `/etc/passwd`: use a number"
findings.fix: Split the claim: "scratch has no /etc/passwd — use a numeric UID. Distroless ships one with a `nonroot` user (65532), so `USER nonroot` or the `:nonroot` tag works."

findings.summary: The last word of a bullet in the 'Never Ship As Root' column is clipped at the column boundary.
findings.evidence: 'scratch/distroless have no /etc/passwd;' — the character after 'passwd' is sliced vertically at the column edge, while neighbouring lines in the same column wrap at a narrower width.
findings.fix: Wrap '/etc/passwd;' to the next line (treat the inline code span as breakable) so it stays inside the left column's text box.

findings.summary: The sticky-note pin covers a character of the HEALTHCHECK code line.
findings.evidence: In 'CMD ["node","health.js"]' the closing ']' is obscured by the pin graphic of the 'shell form swallows SIGTERM' note.
findings.fix: Shift the sticky note and its pin down/left so the pin does not land on the code line's last glyph.
